questions.q: What determines whether Power BI shows Delimiter and Data Type Detection options when you connect to a text file?
options: Whether Power BI detects a consistent delimiter inside the file
Whether the file extension is .csv rather than .txt
The file's size
Whether the file was created in Excel
questions.explain: CSV is really just "text with a detected delimiter." Power BI decides which experience to show based on what it finds inside the file, not its extension.

questions.q: What happens when you load a plain text file with no detectable delimiter?
options: Every line becomes one row in a single text column
Power BI refuses to load the file
Power BI guesses a delimiter anyway, even if it's wrong
It loads as a table with one column per word
questions.explain: With no delimiter to split on, Power BI can't create multiple columns — each line lands in its own row under a single column.

questions.q: What does "Data Type Detection: Based on first 200 rows" mean?
options: Power BI guesses each column's type by sampling only the first 200 rows, which can be wrong if later rows differ
Only the first 200 rows of the file will be loaded
It limits the preview to 200 rows but loads the full file with correct types
It's required for files larger than 200 rows
questions.explain: It's a sampling shortcut for speed. If a column's type changes further down the file, the guess based on the first 200 rows can be wrong — "Based on entire data set" is slower but more reliable.

questions.q: You add three new columns to a CSV file that's already connected to a Power BI report. What happens on the next scheduled refresh?
options: The new columns don't appear — Power BI recorded the original column count at import time
The new columns appear automatically
The refresh fails with an error
Power BI asks you to confirm before adding the new columns
questions.explain: Power BI Desktop generates a fixed column count step at import. Columns added to the source after that aren't picked up by a refresh — you need to reconnect or edit the query.

questions.q: Which Delimiter option would you use for a file where every column is a fixed number of characters wide, with no separator character at all?
options: Fixed width
Comma
--None--
Custom
questions.explain: Fixed width splits columns by a set number of characters instead of looking for a separator character — for files with no delimiter but consistent column widths.
